text:
anita: Quick heads-up: i'm opening a compact PR to standardize the Optimize toolkit examples. Goals: 1) rename kv-prefetch -> kv_cache across examples, 2) add a tiny language parity table (py/js/go/rust), 3) call out a quant-profile short-seq caveat and link to the eval notes. i'll keep PR under 20 LOC per snippet and include link-check. PR shortly: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1701
paul: love it. please include a one-line snippet showing the fallback when kv_cache is off so folks understand runtime prefix caching still helps.
jordy: i saw a discrepancy in our Rust sample earlier  the method name differed from Go. if you're doing a matrix, can you show the exact API call per language? tiny table is perfect.
anita: yep, i'll do a 4-row matrix and add a one-liner note about microbatch boundaries for teams with custom batching logic.
paul: also add a short example combining streaming + batch sizing in the JS sample (`stream: true`, `maxBatch: 8`)  we get a lot of questions about how streaming interacts with batching.
anita: will do; keeping each example under 40 lines. infra-bot: auto-check: PR changed 3 files under /optimize; please ensure console anchors are valid.
anita: thanks infra-bot  i'll run the local link-check and update any console anchors (we recently moved the /optimize/guide path). adding a checklist item to the PR description to open a redirect ticket if anchors change.
jordy: tiny nit: in the quant caveat, specify that short-seq workloads (<32 tokens) saw a small quality drop with the aggressive 4-bit profile in the eval. link the eval so support can triage quickly.
anita: good call; adding a short sentence and pointer to the eval doc. also adding a migration note: teams with custom microbatching should verify boundary alignment after the kv_cache rename.
paul: can you include a one-line test command for running the docs link-check locally? people keep forgetting how to run it.
anita: added: `make docs-linkcheck` under CONTRIBUTING.md and pointed to it in the PR.
triage-bot: label added: docs/optimize, needs-review
paul: happy to review. i'll focus on the language parity table and the JS streaming+batching example.
anita: pushing branch now. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1701. ping here when you start review.
paul: grabbing it. quick read looks good; left one inline about Rust naming.
jordy: approved once the Rust method name is consistent with the API surface.
anita: fixed Rust method (`set_kv_cache(true)`) and updated the table. merging after CI passes. if anyone spots a broken console link post-merge, reply here and i'll include it in the follow-up.
paul: also noted we should update the snippet tags used by the SDK snippets extractor (they changed last quarter). opened a tiny PR in the extractor repo and referenced it in the docs PR.
anita: perfect, added a cross-ref in the PR description. merging on green. :rocket:
